Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: No mandatory data-breach notification requirement could be verified in an official Mauritanian legal text from the available sources; a secondary legal summary claims breach notification obligations exist under Law 2017-020, but a specialized data-law tracker indicates breach notifications to the DPA/data subjects are not required ([Data Protection Africa](https://dataprotection.africa/mauritania/)). Given conflicting evidence and no directly verified primary text on breach notification, this is treated as unknown.

revised_comments: No authoritative source confirms whether Mauritanian payment service providers are subject to a mandatory data breach notification obligation; available legal commentary on the point is contradictory and no primary legislative text resolving the conflict has been identified.

Definition: Whether payment system operators or regulators regularly publish performance metrics and statistics on system usage, transaction volumes/values, participant numbers, uptime, and other operational indicators.
Comments: No recurring public performance reporting (monthly/quarterly/annual) found for GIMTEL or a national IPS (e.g., uptime, transaction volumes, SLA metrics); searches for BCM/GIMTEL payment statistics and performance dashboards did not yield official public reports.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Reclassified from Unknown (0) to Ad Hoc (2). GIMTEL's public website (gimtel.mr) was fetched and confirmed to publish a set of headline operational figures under 'Les chiffres clés': approximately 500,000 transactions per year, 225 participating merchants, 282 ATMs, 17 member banks, and 120,000 cards produced per year. This is a static summary rather than a periodic (annual/quarterly) performance report with dated figures, uptime or SLA metrics, so it does not meet the bar for Annual (3) or Monthly/Quarterly (4) reporting. No dedicated BCM or GIMTEL payment-system performance report or dashboard was found.
revised_comments: GIMTEL, Mauritania's national card and payments switch, publishes a small set of headline operational statistics on its public website, including annual transaction volume (approximately 500,000 transactions per year), number of participating merchants (225), ATMs (282), member banks (17), and cards produced per year (120,000). These figures appear as static headline statistics on the homepage rather than as a periodic performance report, and no uptime, SLA or dated time-series data are published.

Definition: Whether payment system governance explicitly includes mechanisms to ensure inclusivity and represent interests of vulnerable populations, including provisions for input from all participant types, consumer representatives, small providers, or explicit financial inclusion mandates in governance documents.
Comments: No credible public evidence found of formal pro-poor governance mechanisms (e.g., mandated consumer/low-income representation, explicit inclusion committees within scheme governance) for Mauritania's national switch or IPS; searched for “financial inclusion governance” and “payment system governance” references tied to GIMTEL/BCM but only found general statements of intent.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Tentatively reclassified from Unknown (0) to No (1). The Alliance for Financial Inclusion's 2024 case study on financial inclusion of forcibly displaced persons in Mauritania (fetched via search and reviewed in detail) states explicitly that GIMTEL, the national payment switch, 'is not currently well-positioned to ensure financial inclusion of those with modest means', and notes the absence of a mobile-money framework or national e-payments strategy. No governance mechanism (consumer advisory board, small-PSP board seat, inclusion mandate in scheme charter) is documented for GIMTEL or any national payment scheme; the National Financial Inclusion Strategy (SNIF 2023-2028) sets inclusion targets at policy level but does not describe payment-scheme governance provisions specifically. This inference is drawn from a statement about outcomes/positioning rather than an explicit statement about the absence of governance structures, so flagged for human review rather than asserted with full confidence.
revised_comments: Available evidence indicates that Mauritania's national payment infrastructure lacks formal pro-poor governance mechanisms. The Alliance for Financial Inclusion's 2024 assessment of financial inclusion for displaced persons found that GIMTEL, the national card and payments switch, is not well positioned to serve those with modest means, and no mobile-money or e-payments strategy with explicit inclusion governance (such as consumer representation, small-provider board seats, or an inclusion mandate) has been identified. Financial inclusion targets exist at national strategy level (the National Financial Inclusion Strategy, SNIF 2023-2028) but are not embedded in payment-scheme governance structures.

Definition: Percentage of government payments (G2P disbursements including salaries, pensions, social transfers) made through instant digital payment system rather than cash or check, reflecting government adoption and modernization.
Comments: No credible quantified estimate found for the share of government payments digitized in Mauritania (e.g., % of salaries/transfers paid digitally); searches found planning/feasibility activities but not a digitization rate.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Tentatively reclassified from Unknown. The Central Bank of Mauritania's retail payments diagnostic (prepared with the World Bank, published December 2017, data year 2016; fetched and read) found that Government-to-Person (G2P) payments, valued at MRO 132.33 billion, were 'for the most part digitised', with approximately 99% of value paid by bank transfer (virement) rather than cash. This directly supports a high digitisation score (5 = >89%) for that year. However, this figure is a decade old and predates subsequent developments (the BCM's AMWALI government e-payment portal, and GIMTEL's 2024 interoperable mobile-wallet platform), and it measures digitisation via ordinary bank transfer rather than a defined 'instant payment system' as the current variable specifies. Flagged for human review given the data's age and the ambiguity between general 'digital' transfer and a specific 'instant payment system'; a fresher, system-specific figure was not found.
revised_comments: The most recent quantified estimate available is from the Central Bank of Mauritania's 2016/17 retail payments diagnostic, which found that government-to-person disbursements (valued at approximately MRO 132 billion) were almost entirely digitised, with about 99% of value paid via bank transfer rather than cash. More recent initiatives, including the BCM's AMWALI e-payment portal for government service charges and GIMTEL's 2024 interoperable mobile-wallet platform, indicate continued government investment in digital payment channels, though a current system-specific digitisation percentage is not available.
